blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Cultural attitudes and social norms evolve over time, yet most cultural benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) treat culture as a static attribute of a country or region. We introduce ChronoCulture, a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal survey data across 72 countries. Each pair contains the same survey question asked in the same country in an older and a newer year, with full population response distributions as ground truth. Across six LLMs, we find that models can often predict a country's attitudes at one point in time but do not reliably capture how those attitudes change. Their predictions for different years tend to stay close together, failing to capture much of the observed change. Specifying the intended year in the prompt also offers little overall improvement in alignment with survey responses. These findings suggest that models often present a largely static picture of cultural attitudes, highlighting the need to evaluate cultural awareness across time.
blocks.zh: 文化态度和社会规范随时间演变,但大多数大语言模型(LLMS)的文化基准将文化视为一个国家或区域的静态属性. 我们介绍了ChronoCurture,这是根据72个国家的纵向调查数据制定的10,360对时间基准。 每对调查都包含同一国家中在较老和较新年份提出的相同调查问题,人口答复分布全面,作为地面真相。 我们发现,在六个法学硕士课程中,模型往往能够预测一个国家在某一时刻的态度,但却不能可靠地反映这些态度是如何改变的。 他们对不同年份的预测往往保持紧密的距离,无法捕捉到观察到的许多变化. 及时指明预定年份,在与调查答复保持一致方面也没有多少总体改进。 这些调查结果表明,模型往往呈现出文化态度的大致静态图景,突出表明有必要对文化意识进行长期评价。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in settings that require cultural awareness, from globalized communication and education to social science and anthropology research. This has motivated a growing line of benchmarks that test whether models can represent cultural views and social norms across diverse countries and communities ( Myung et al., 2024 ; Chiu et al., 2025 ; Alwajih et al., 2025a ; Li et al., 2024 ) . However, most existing benchmarks treat culture as a fixed rather than evolving characteristic of a country or community, thereby evaluating models against a single cultural snapshot.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型越来越多地被部署在需要文化意识的环境中,从全球化的传播和教育到社会科学和人类学研究。 这促使越来越多的基准测试模型是否能够代表不同国家和社区的文化观点和社会规范(Myung等,2024;Chiu等,2025;Alwajih等,2025a;Li等,2024)。 然而,大多数现有基准将文化视为一个国家或社区的固定特征,而不是不断变化的特征,从而对照单一的文化概况来评价模式。

blocks.en:
In reality, cultural attitudes and social norms are not static. They may evolve over time in response to economic development, generational change, and political transformation ( Inglehart, 1997 ; Inglehart, 2018 ) . The extent of this change can also vary across societies: attitudes toward religion, gender roles, or trust may remain relatively stable in some countries while changing substantially in others ( Inglehart and Baker, 2000 ) .
This raises a central question: can language models represent how cultural attitudes evolve over time?

实际上,文化态度和社会规范并非一成不变。 它们可能随时间推移而演变,以适应经济发展、代际变化和政治变革(Inglehart,1997;Inglehart,2018)。 这种变化的程度也可能因社会而异:一些国家对宗教、性别角色或信任的态度可能保持相对稳定,而另一些国家则大有变化(Inglehart和Baker,2000年)。
这提出了一个中心问题:语言模式能否代表文化态度如何随时间演变?

blocks.en: 2 Related Works
blocks.zh: 2 相关工程

blocks.en: Existing cultural benchmarks evaluate LLMs on everyday knowledge and commonsense ( Myung et al., 2024 ; Chang et al., 2025 ; Singh et al., 2025 ) , cultural values and norms ( Naous et al., 2024 ; Chiu et al., 2025 ; Rao et al., 2025 ; Qiu et al., 2025 ) , and multimodal cultural knowledge ( Schneider et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Tan et al., 2026 ; Faraz et al., 2026 ) . However, these benchmarks largely treat culture as a static attribute of a country, language, or region ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Alkhamissi et al., 2026 ) . We instead treat culture as evolving over time and examine whether LLMs capture changes in cultural attitudes.
blocks.zh: 现有的文化基准评价了关于日常知识和常识(Myung等人,2024年;Chang等人,2025年;Singh等人,2025年)、文化价值和规范(Naous等人,2024年;Chiu等人,2025年;Rao等人,2025年;Quu等人,2025年)和多模式文化知识的法学硕士课程。 (Schneider等,2025;Li等,2026;Tan等,2026;Faraz等,2026). 然而,这些基准基本上将文化视为一个国家、语言或地区的静态属性(周等,2025;Alkhamisi等,2026)。 相反,我们把文化视为随着时间推移而演变,并审查LLMS是否反映了文化态度的变化。

blocks.en:
Temporal QA benchmarks primarily focus on changing factual knowledge, such as historical events and entity attributes ( Chen et al., 2021 ; Tang et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2025 ; Piryani et al., 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ) . Related vision-language research examines whether models can interpret
cultural content from different historical periods, including films,
artifacts, and cultural heritage images ( Jajoo et al., 2025 ; Ghaboura et al., 2025 ; Ranjan et al., 2026 ) .
We instead evaluate whether text-based LLMs capture changes in
population attitudes, using longitudinal survey responses.

blocks.en: 3 Benchmark Creation
blocks.zh: 3 基准创建

blocks.en: We introduce ChronoCulture, a benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can represent cultural attitudes at different time periods and capture how those attitudes change. It contains survey questions asked in the same countries at different time periods, so that each cultural topic can be examined over time within the same country.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍了ChronoCurture,这是评估有限责任公司是否能够在不同时期代表文化态度并了解这些态度如何变化的基准。 它包含在不同时间段向同一国家提出的调查问题,以便可以在同一国家内逐一审查每个文化专题。

blocks.en:
We construct the benchmark using three design principles. First, we
ground cultural attitudes in people’s survey responses for a given
country and year, drawing on surveys conducted across countries over multiple years. Second, we use full response distributions as ground truth rather than a single mean or majority answer,
preserving the diversity of opinions within each population. Third, we compare the same question within the same country across time, forming temporal pairs of response distributions from two survey years.

cultural attitudes change.

This allows us to assess whether models capture the extent
of that change. We measure this change using the Wasserstein
distance ( Villani, 2009 ; Peyré and Cuturi, 2019 ) between G old G_{\mathrm{old}} and G new G_{\mathrm{new}} , which takes the order of
response options into account.
Because questions have different numbers of response options,
we normalize the distance to a common [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] range.
We denote this normalized Wasserstein distance by W W and define the human shift , d h d_{h} , as: d h = W ⁡ ( G old , G new ) . d_{h}=W\left(G_{\mathrm{old}},G_{\mathrm{new}}\right). (1) Larger values indicate greater changes in cultural attitudes.

blocks.en: 3.6 Why Distribution Evaluation?

blocks.en: Following our second design principle, we evaluate cultural change using full response distributions, since evaluations based on a single correct answer may miss shifts in population attitudes. To examine this limitation, we construct an MCQ version of our benchmark, treating each response option as a choice and the most common population response (the mode) as the correct answer.
blocks.zh: 按照我们的第二项设计原则,我们利用充分的响应分布来评价文化变化,因为基于单一正确答案的评价可能会错过人口态度的转变。 为了审查这一局限性,我们构建了我们基准的MCQ版本,将每个响应选项作为选择,并将最常见的人群响应(模式)作为正确的答案.

blocks.en: Figure 4 illustrates two limitations. A substantial shift in the response distribution may leave the mode unchanged, causing the MCQ evaluation to miss the shift (false negative). Conversely, a slight shift may change the mode, causing the evaluation to overstate the change (false positive). Thus, modal answers alone cannot reliably measure the magnitude of cultural change.

blocks.en: Recent work has explored direct prompting of response distributions from LLMs, asking models to output numerical distributions over answer options in structured formats ( Suzuki et al., 2025 ; Meister et al., 2025 ) . They show that directly prompting an LLM for a response distribution outperforms repeated individual querying ( Meister et al., 2025 ; Gong et al., 2026 ) . blocks.en: 4 Experiments and Results
blocks.zh: 4 实验和结果

blocks.en: A temporally aware model should reflect cultural attitudes as they change over time, while producing similar predictions when those attitudes remain stable. We first apply a knowledge filter to retain questions for which models show baseline cultural knowledge (Section 4.1 ). We then present three Research Findings (RFs): (1) predicting both periods accurately becomes harder as cultural change increases (Section 4.2 ), (2) models follow the direction of larger cultural shifts but underestimate their magnitude (Section 4.3 ) and (3) naming a year does not consistently improve alignment (Section 4.4 ). Finally, in Section 4.5 , we examine how temporal performance varies across topics and regions.
blocks.zh: 时间意识模型应反映文化态度随时间而变化,同时在这种态度保持稳定时作出类似的预测。 我们首先使用知识过滤器来保留模型显示基本文化知识的问题(第4.1节)。 然后,我们提出三项研究结果:(一) 随着文化变化的增加,准确预测这两个时期变得更加困难(第4.2节),(二) 模式遵循更大的文化转变方向,但低估其规模(第4.3节),(三) 一年命名不能持续改善一致性(第4.4节)。 最后,在第4.5节中,我们审查不同专题和区域的时间业绩如何不同。

blocks.en: 4.1 Cultural Knowledge Filter
blocks.zh: 4.1 文化知识过滤器

blocks.en: Our goal is to evaluate whether models can accurately predict cultural attitudes across different time periods. However, poor predictions could also imply limited knowledge, rather than an inability to track how cultural attitudes change. Thus, before evaluating temporal awareness, we apply a filter to only retain questions for which the model shows some evidence of baseline knowledge.
blocks.zh: 我们的目标是评价模型是否能够准确预测不同时期的文化态度。 然而,不良的预测也可能意味着知识有限,而不是无法跟踪文化态度的改变。 因此,在评估时间意识之前,我们使用过滤器只保留模型显示一些基线知识证据的问题。

blocks.en: To apply this filter, we estimate the model’s baseline knowledge by comparing its predictions with observed survey responses. For each question–country combination, we prompt the model to predict the response distribution without specifying a year, giving the undated prediction P undated P_{\mathrm{undated}} . We compute the Wasserstein distance between P undated P_{\mathrm{undated}} and the gold distribution for each available survey year, and define K K as the minimum of these distances. A small K K means the model’s prediction aligns with the cultural attitudes of at least one year, suggesting some baseline knowledge.

blocks.en: 4.5 Findings by Topic and Region
blocks.zh: 4.5 按主题和区域分列的调查结果

blocks.en: We now highlight key findings on temporal awareness across topics and regions. Appendix C.4 provides the full results.
blocks.zh: 我们现在强调关于各专题和区域时间意识的关键结论。 附录C.4提供了全部结果。

blocks.en: For strong and very strong cultural shifts, predictions are less accurate for political and economic topics than for family and personal life. For example, both-period accuracy for democracy and social inequality is roughly half that for family and life priorities. Likewise, models predict the observed direction of change in only about 50% of cases for democracy and social inequality, compared with 82–94% for family and life priorities. Notably, democracy is among the most accurately predicted WVS topics for stable pairs (71%), yet its accuracy drops to 17% for larger shifts.
blocks.zh: 对于强烈和非常强烈的文化转变,对政治和经济议题的预测不如对家庭和个人生活的预测准确。 例如,民主和社会不平等的两期准确度约为家庭和生活优先事项的一半。 同样,模型预测的只有50%左右的民主和社会不平等情况的变化方向,而家庭和生活优先事项的变化趋势为82-94%。 特别是,民主是稳定对等(71%)最准确预测的WVS主题之一,但对于较大的班次,民主的准确性下降到了17%。

blocks.en: Regional differences grow with the magnitude of cultural shift. For stable WVS pairs, we find that Western countries, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), and Sub-Saharan Africa show similar accuracy (71–73%). Under strong and very strong shifts, however, both-period accuracy is higher in Western countries (35%) than in MENA and South and Southeast Asia (16% on average). This gap between countries under larger shifts is smaller in ISSP, with 30% accuracy in Western countries versus 23–29% in other regions. Thus, models predict stable attitudes quite accurately across all regions, but for larger shifts, accuracy declines more sharply outside Western countries.
blocks.zh: 区域差异随着文化转变的扩大而扩大。 对于稳定的WVS配对,我们发现西方国家,中东和北非(MENA)和撒哈拉以南非洲也表现出类似的准确性(71-73%). 然而,在强而强的转变下,西方国家的两期准确度(35%)高于中东和北非以及南亚和东南亚(平均16%)。 在ISSP中,较大变化国家之间的差距较小,西方国家为30%,而其他地区为23-29%。 因此,模型对所有区域的稳定态度的预测相当准确,但对于更大的转变,准确性在西方国家以外更大幅度地下降。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We asked whether language models can represent not only what a
population believes, but also how those beliefs change over time.
Across six models, this ability remains limited. Models often capture a
country’s attitudes at one point in time, yet present its evolving
culture as largely static: their predictions for different years tend
to stay close together. Furthermore, when attitudes shift strongly, models
capture the direction of change better than its magnitude. This gap
appears across all topics and regions, and is widest for political and
economic topics and for many non-Western populations.

blocks.en: 6 Limitations
blocks.zh: 6 限制

blocks.en: ChronoCulture evaluates cultural attitudes using longitudinal survey data from the WVS and ISSP, so its coverage is limited to the countries, topics, and years included in these programs. At the time of writing, Wave 8 of the WVS has not been released, and our benchmark therefore does not capture changes in cultural attitudes after 2022. We also focus on questions with consistent, ordered response options across survey years, examining changes in reported attitudes and values rather than other aspects of culture, such as everyday customs and material culture.
blocks.zh: ChronoCurture使用来自WVS和ISSP的纵向调查数据来评价文化态度,因此其覆盖范围仅限于这些方案所包含的国家,主题和年份. 在写作时,WVS的"第8波"还没有发布,因此我们的基准无法捕捉2022年后文化态度的变化. 我们还注重在调查年中始终如一、有条不紊地作出反应的问题,审查所报告的态度和价值观的变化,而不是文化的其他方面,例如日常习俗和物质文化。

blocks.en:
We represent each population by its country-level response distribution. Although these distributions preserve the diversity of opinions within a country, they can hide differences between demographic, regional, or cultural groups within countries. Future extensions of ChronoCulture could incorporate
newer survey waves and finer-grained population data to examine
cultural change across more periods and communities.

blocks.en: F.3 Robustness to Repeated Runs and Prompt Instructions
blocks.zh: F.3 对重复运行和快速指令的强性

blocks.en:
We examine inference stability and sensitivity to elicitation instructions
using Llama-3.3-70B on 300 temporal pairs, sampled equally across the four
human-shift categories without applying the knowledge filter. First, we
repeat each original prompt five times. Predictions are identical to the
first run in 90.5% of comparisons, with a mean distance of 0.0026,
indicating limited run-to-run variation. Second, we test two alternative
instructions that frame the task as estimating responses from a nationally
representative survey or from 100 adults. The survey questions and response
options remain unchanged, and within each temporal pair only the year
differs. Although these instructions affect individual predictions (mean
distances of 0.069 and 0.060 from the original instruction), the main
temporal patterns persist. Under all three instructions, both-period
accuracy declines with human shift, median magnitude ratios remain below 1
and are lower for strong and very strong shifts than for moderate shifts,
and directional alignment is highest for very strong shifts. Identical
predictions between periods also persist, although their frequency varies
across instructions.

blocks.en: F.4 Survey Sampling Noise
blocks.zh: F.4 调查抽样噪音

blocks.en:
Gold distributions are estimated from samples of respondents, so some
difference between years can arise from sampling alone. To estimate this
noise, we assume for each temporal pair that the older gold distribution
did not change, draw two independent samples of 500 respondents from it
(the minimum sample size in our benchmark), and compute the distance
between them, repeating this 200 times. Sampling alone produces a median
distance of 0.016, and the 95th percentile of these distances has a median
of 0.034 across pairs. Our stable threshold of 0.03 therefore corresponds
to differences that sampling alone can produce. All strong and very strong
shifts and 90.1% of moderate shifts exceed the 95th percentile of their
own pair. Since most surveys include more than 500 respondents, these
estimates are conservative.
